As the leading company in the field of software solutions for healthcare, we operate in 19 countries and employ over 9,000 dedicated staff members. You will work in a dynamic and innovative environment full of opportunities. With your commitment and passion, you have the chance to make a sustainable difference.  

**CGM Leverages AI:** We’re looking for people who feel the power of AI in the e-health environment, who want to help shape change, and who are driven by a curious passion to see how technology can make healthcare smarter, simpler, and better. 

Together, we are shaping the healthcare system of the future. Become part of our mission and make a difference – **for a world where knowledge saves lives!** 

Are you passionate about groundbreaking products? Do you have the talent to turn ideas into real, valuable solutions—while always keeping the bigger picture in mind? Then we’d love to meet you! 

Your Impact:

- You provide professional, organizational, and people leadership for multiple software development teams and build a culture of innovation, collaboration, mentoring, and proactive ownership.
- You define and drive development strategies that focus on robust SaaS architectures and cloud technologies to maximise scalability, flexibility and time‑to‑market.
- You establish AI‑native engineering as a standard—leveraging Claude Code, agents, skills, workflows, pipelines, harnesses and context engineering—and make AI‑driven productivity gains measurable across teams
- You ensure that processes, quality, and security standards are consistently met, with rigorous attention to healthcare regulatory requirements and compliance.
- You synchronize product requirements with business-area objectives, mentor engineering leaders, and regularly communicate progress, risks, and innovations to executive management.

Your Profile:

- Extensive experience in software development leadership roles, particularly in the SaaS domain and ideally in the healthcare industry, with a strong track record of successful delivery in cloud environments.
- Excellent university degree in computer science, software engineering, medical informatics, or a comparable technical field with very strong academic performance.
- Strong technical acumen in SaaS architecture, cloud and distributed systems, security, and quality automation, plus a proven track record of driving AI adoption in engineering teams, ideally including hands‑on familiarity with Claude Code or similar agentic tooling (agents, skills, workflows, pipelines, harnesses, and context engineering).
- Deep experience with Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban) and Lean Management principles and the ability to scale these across multiple teams.
- Excellent English and very good German; outstanding leadership and communication skills, strong problem‑solving capabilities, high innovation drive and proactivity, and a clear alignment with our healthcare purpose and entrepreneurial mindset.

**What you can expect from us:**  

- Mobile work: Work flexibly on the move two days a week and on site three days a week. 
- **Attractive locations:** In addition to fully equipped workplaces, regular events such as summer parties and Christmas parties await you at our locations. 
- **Development:** Our in-house academy and our portfolio of external cooperation partners will support you in your further development. 
- **Health:** Health is a valuable asset for us. Our in-house canteen offers a selection of tasty and healthy dishes every day, and we welcome you to our fully equipped fitness center for weekly courses (online & offline). 
- More is always possible: The kindergarten on our CGM campus in Koblenz helps our employees to organize their working day even more flexibly. We also offer corporate benefits, the option of a job bike, a company pension scheme, and much more. 

**Diversity is part of CGM!** We look forward to receiving your application regardless of disability, gender, nationality, ethnic and social background, religion, age, sexual orientation, and identity. 

**Convinced?** Apply online now with your detailed application documents (including salary expectations and earliest possible starting date).

The Research Engineer will contribute to driving R&D initiatives within a dynamic industrial setting, focusing on the development of new products, services, and basic knowledge of steel casting fluxes (mold powder for continuous casting of steel) and raw materials. The role encompasses applications in continuous casting of steel. This position bridges laboratory research and plant operations, emphasizing sustainable solutions, process efficiencies, and delivering high-quality results for industrial clients worldwide.

Responsibilities:

1. Project Management :

- Define research programs aligned with new product and service objectives.
- Organize and execute laboratory-scale R&D projects.
- Performs tasks/projects and takes the responsibility for assuring quality, cost effectiveness & timeliness for those projects
- Develop materials and processes while supporting related projects.
- Maintain regular reporting on project progress and outcomes.
- Supervise customer sample preparation and optimize products based on feedback.
- Monitor technical advancements in the market, including patents and scientific publications.
- Consolidate fundamental knowledge on steel casting fluxes and associated raw materials.

2. Laboratory Research and Data Management :

- Plan research activities, including experiments, characterization, and analytics
- Manage, process, analyse, and document data from lab activities.
- Maximize data collection value from R&D, production, and quality assurance.
- Develop project reviews, technical reports, and presentations with clarity and precision.
- Document knowledge and findings in technical memos and share them with stakeholders.
- Utilize project management tools (e.g., Vantage) for deliverables and resource planning.
- Organize stage-gate meetings and prioritize multiple projects.

3. External Collaboration and Scientific Contributions :

- Prepare papers, proposals, and presentations for conferences, congresses, and seminars.
- Build external collaborations and networks to share and extend expertise.
- Address intellectual property topics, support evaluations, and assist in patent filings.

Requirements: 

- PhD or master’s degree in Materials Science, Metallurgy, Mineralogy, or a related engineering discipline, preferably with a focus on casting fluxes (mold powders), glass chemistry, and/or interactions between slag and liquid steel.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in R&D, project management, or product development, ideally within or for a steel plant environment.
- Comprehensive knowledge of continuous steel casting processes, mineralogy, and ceramic raw materials for casting fluxes, including their melting and solidification mechanisms under high-temperature conditions.
- Strong expertise in thermodynamics and reaction kinetics, with proficiency in thermodynamic calculation tools (e.g., FactSage®).
- Hands-on experience with advanced analytical techniques, such as high-temperature viscometry, hot-stage microscopy, TG/DTA, XRD, and Rietveld refinement.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities, with demonstrated experience in data analysis and interpretation.
- Strong technical writing and presentation skills, including the ability to clearly summarize research outcomes and present results during stage-gate or project review meetings.
- Motivated, adaptable, and innovative, with a proactive approach to challenges and a strong drive for continuous improvement.
- Collaborative mindset, with the ability to work effectively in an international environment and partner across R&D and plant operations.
- Fluency in German and English, both written and spoken.

The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.

The following part-time (65% = 25.025 hours/week) position is to be filled as of October 1, 2026, in the Department of Epileptology of the University Hospital Bonn:

PhD Position (m/f/d)

The position is limited to 3 years.

The PhD position is focusing on pathomechanisms in autoantibody-associated neurological syndromes and autoimmune encephalitis and and supported by a grant from the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG). I will focus on the question whether (1) intracellular autoantibodies contribute causally to encephalitis, rather than acting as mere passive biomarkers and how (2) patient-derived Abs from autoantibody-positive encephalitis patients with different neurological presentations affect neuronal function using cultured neurons to assess cellular uptake, enzyme activity, neurotransmitter release and changes in neuronal plasticity.

This research is based on a wide array of methods including in vitro (e. g. Pitsch et al., 2020, PMID: 32196746) and mouse models (viral vector gene transfer/transgenic, EEG/video recordings) approaches, cell biological, molecular, biochemical, histological as well as imaging techniques (e. g. Pitsch et al., 2021, PMID: 33368582). A better understanding of the molecular and functional consequences of intracellular autoantibodies will have direct implications for better therapies aimed at interfering with autoimmune encephalitis by using pathway-specific pharmaceuticals or gene therapy.

Interested candidates should send curriculum vitae, letter of motivation indicating starting date, short description of past lab experience, copies of university degree(s) with academic records, contact information and at least two reference letters (or the referee’s contact info).

Questions concerning the projects can be addressed to PD Dr. J. Pitsch (Julika.Pitsch@ukbonn.de)

Tasks:

- - The ideal candidate will be an ambitious, highly motivated, team-oriented graduate student with a strong interest in immunology and neurobiology

Requirements:

- Prior research experience with animal experimentation, microscopy, or electrophysiology techniques is advantageous but not required.
- Candidates should hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in Neuroscience, Biological Science, Pharmacy, Veterinary Medicine, or a related field.
- Candidates should also demonstrate aptitude in written and spoken English.

**We offer:** 

- **Responsible and diverse:** A position with plenty of room for creativity and responsibility within a supportive and collegial team
- **Fair compensation:** Pay according to the TV-L E13 (65%) collective agreement, including annual bonus and company pension scheme

- **Structured onboarding:** A systematic introduction to your new role and team
- **Healthy at work:** A wide range of health and wellness programs, plus free membership at the UKB fitness studio
- **Employee benefits:** Access to discounted offers for employees (corporate benefits)

We are committed to diversity and equal opportunities. Our goal is to increase the proportion of women in areas where women are underrepresented and to particularly promote their careers. Applications from suitable people with proven severe disabilities and those of equal status are particularly welcome.

Research Associate / Project Coordinator (m/f/d)

The Department of Health Services Research at the Institute of Diversity Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Ruhr University Bochum, Germany, is seeking to appoint a Research Associate / Project Coordinator (m/f/d) starting 1st of January 2027. The Department of Health Services Research investigates how individual diversity characteristics influence healthcare delivery and develops, implements, and evaluates innovative, patient-centred models of care. Our research focuses on the evaluation of complex interventions, participatory health services research, and the development of diversity-sensitive healthcare concepts. Our interdisciplinary work integrates health services research, public health, social sciences, and medical ethics.

The successful candidate will join the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's Programme DIME – Diversity Medicine, an international initiative to establish a new joint Master's programme together with leading European and international partner universities (e.g. France, Japan, Taiwan). This position offers the unique opportunity to contribute to the development of an innovative international degree programme at the intersection of diversity medicine, global health, and higher education. As Research Associate / Project Coordinator, you will play a central role in coordinating this international consortium. You will collaborate closely with academic partners, university leadership, teaching staff, students, and funding organisations across several countries. The position requires excellent English proficiency, strong interpersonal and diplomatic skills, and outstanding organisational abilities to successfully coordinate complex international collaborations.

Duration: fixed-term, 15 Monate

- Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings
- support the coordination of academic activities within DIME, including communication with partner universities, students and visiting academics

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher Position— Plant Membrane Biochemistry and Chemoproteomics (m/f/d)  (10/2026) (UX-Researcher/in)
jobs.description:
Your area of responsibility The question How does proteolytic regulation control plant plasma-membrane receptor function and plant immune responses? The plant plasma membrane is a dynamic hub for nutrient uptake, pathogen detection and stress signalling, anchored by surface receptors. In animals, proteolytic cleavage of membrane proteins is a major regulatory mechanism in immunity. In plants, its role remains largely unexplored. FRONTERA, funded by the European Research Council through an ERC Starting Grant, sets out to close that gap. The project combines chemoproteomics, cell biology, protease biochemistry and genetics, and looks at both sides of the process: the proteases that cut, and the substrates they act on. It is curiosity-driven research with a long view towards crop resilience and sustainable agriculture. Your tasks: You will lead the membrane biochemistry and chemoproteomics side of FRONTERA: establishing the preparations and the activity-based profiling needed to study proteases where they work, at the plant plasma membrane.
• Develop and optimise membrane preparation methods suited to downstream chemoproteomics
• Apply activity-based protein profiling and mass spectrometry to characterise membrane-associated protease activities, working with our in-house facility
• Relate biochemical findings to immune responses in planta, in collaboration across the group
• Co-supervise a doctoral researcher
• Present and publish your scientific data

Your profile Essential
• A doctoral degree in biochemistry, plant science, molecular biology, chemical biology or a closely related field. If your thesis is submitted but not yet defended by the start date, please apply and tell us your timeline.
• Solid hands-on experience in protein biochemistry
• Real interest in method development, including tolerance for the weeks when a protocol refuses to work
• Interest in mentoring a doctoral researcher
• Excellent English language skills, written and spoken. German is not required.

Desirable
• Membrane protein handling, subcellular fractionation or membrane isolation
• Activity-based protein profiling, chemical probes or related chemical biology
• LC-MS/MS proteomics, from sample preparation to data analysis
• Work with plant systems, including transient expression
• Proteomics data analysis (MaxQuant, FragPipe, Perseus, R, Python)
• Supervision or teaching experience

Read the second list as a description of the project, not a test. Nobody arrives with all of it. Candidates who would do this job well routinely talk themselves out of applying because they match four points instead of six. If the science interests you and you bring the essentials, we would like to see your application. Tell us in your cover letter what you would need to learn.

We offer
• Modern Working Conditions: Comprehensive introduction to work techniques and a modern research environment with state-of-the-art equipment and up-to-date software
• Career Development: Targeted training opportunities and access to a specialized library with electronic resources and quiet workspaces
• Compensation & Security: Classification according to TV-L including annual bonus, pension scheme (VBL), health offers, and discounted canteen meals
• Ideal Working Environment: A varied and inspiring workplace in an international setting at a leading scientific and innovation hub
• Team Spirit and Leadership Culture: An open culture that strengthens teamwork, enables career networking, and promotes your research skills.
• Work-Life Balance: Flexible working models, remote work options, and 30 days of annual leave – for a balanced work-life experience.

About us The Independent Research Group Receptor Biochemistry, led by Dr. Mariana Schuster, is dedicated to understanding and engineering the molecular decisions that determine whether a plant gets sick, focusing on the proteases deployed by plants and pathogens and the proteins they cut. We are small, international and deliberately interdisciplinary. People here come from plant science, biochemistry, chemistry and computational backgrounds, and much of the useful thinking happens in the conversations between them. The IPB is a non-university research institute of the Leibniz Association on the Weinberg Campus of Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, a foundation under public law under the direct supervision of the state of Saxony-Anhalt. Around 200 people work here, including about 40 doctoral researchers, across four scientific departments and two independent research groups. Research at the IPB aims to understand the (bio)chemical basis of plant resilience and performance in challenging environments related to climate change. The IPB offers excellent research facilities and state-of-the-art infrastructure, including in-house mass spectrometry. More at ipb-halle.de. Halle (Saale) is a green, walkable city with a large student population, low living costs by German standards, and fast connections to Leipzig and Berlin.

Dr. Mariana Schuster
Head of Research Group
Telefon:
Mariana.Schuster@ipb-halle.de

Leibniz-Institut für Pflanzenbiochemie (IPB)
Weinberg 3
06120 Halle (Saale)

The Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, with its tradition spanning more than 600 years, is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With over 1,300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and serves as a training center for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and midwifery.

We are seeking a highly motivated Epidemiologist to design and conduct epidemiological research in pediatric populations, focusing on the determinants of child health, the development of common childhood diseases, particularly obesity, and the prevention and long-term outcomes of childhood obesity and metabolic diseases.
The research group "Childhood Obesity and Metabolic Research", led by Antje Körner, investigates the development, mechanisms and health consequences of childhood obesity. The translational approach combines experimental research, clinical studies and genetic approaches. Our international and interdisciplinary team is closely integrated with the research structures of the Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, Helmholtz Munich, and leading local as well as national research consortia, such as the Excellence cluster LeiCeM, the German Center for Child and Youth Health (DZKJ), and our large children's and adolescents' cohort LIFE Child.
We have large, well-characterized cohorts up and running with a longitudinal setting and across the entire age range: LIFE Child (n~6000), Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort (n~2500), and Leipzig Adipose Tissue Childhood cohort (n~700), with deep phenotyping allowing for combining clinical, epidemiological, lifestyle and functional omics and multi-omics data.
